family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: Format an integer n as a zero-padded string of at least the given width: pad with leading zeros so the digits occupy width characters, keeping a leading minus sign (not counted in the zero-padding of digits) for negative numbers. If str(n) is already at least width characters long, return it unchanged.
reference:
def zero_pad_id(n, width):
    return str(n).zfill(width)

family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: Given a string prefix, an integer n, and a padding width, return the prefix concatenated with n zero-padded to the given width, for example prefix 'INV-' with n 123 and width 6 becomes 'INV-000123'.
reference:
def format_id_prefixed(prefix, n, width):
    return prefix + str(n).zfill(width)

family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: Given an integer n, a padding width, and a suffix string, return n zero-padded to the given width followed immediately by the suffix, for example n 42 with width 5 and suffix '-A' becomes '00042-A'.
reference:
def format_id_suffixed(n, width, suffix):
    return str(n).zfill(width) + suffix

family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: Generate a list of count sequential ids starting at start, each formatted as the given prefix followed by the number zero-padded to width. For example prefix 'A-', start 1, count 3, width 3 produces ['A-001', 'A-002', 'A-003']. A count of 0 produces an empty list.
reference:
def sequential_ids(prefix, start, count, width):
    return [prefix + str(start + i).zfill(width) for i in range(count)]

family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: Zero-pad the integer n to the given width, then compute a check digit as the sum of the padded numeric digits modulo 10, and append that single check digit to the end. Negative numbers keep their zero-padded minus sign but the check digit is still based only on the digit characters.

family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: Format a non-negative integer n as a lowercase hexadecimal string zero-padded on the left to at least the given width. For example n 255 with width 4 becomes '00ff'.
reference:
def format_hex_id(n, width):
    return format(n, f"0{width}x")

family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: Zero-pad the non-negative integer n to the given width, then split the resulting digit string into consecutive chunks of the given group size (the last chunk may be shorter) and join the chunks with hyphens.

family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: Given a digit-only id string (possibly zero-padded), strip its leading zeros; if the string was entirely zeros, treat the resulting value as '0'. Then re-pad the resulting digits to new_width with leading zeros. If new_width is smaller than the stripped digit count, the digits are returned unpadded and unshortened.

family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: Lowercase the entire string, then find the first alphabetic character in the result and make it uppercase, leaving every other character as lowered. If the string has no alphabetic characters, return the fully lowered string unchanged.
visible_tests: assert sentence_case('the Quick FOX') == 'The quick fox'
hidden_tests: assert sentence_case('123 not letters first') == '123 Not letters first'
assert sentence_case('   leading spaces then Text') == '   Leading spaces then text'

assert sentence_case('ONE TWO THREE') == 'One two three'
assert sentence_case('42 is the answer') == '42 Is the answer'
assert sentence_case('café already accented') == 'Café already accented'
assert sentence_case('Z last letter first z') == 'Z last letter first z'
assert sentence_case('x Y z') == 'X y z'

family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: Split text into sentence fragments wherever '. ' (a period followed by a space) occurs. For each fragment, lowercase it and then uppercase its first alphabetic character (fragments with no letters stay fully lowered). Rejoin the fixed fragments with '. '.
visible_tests: assert sentence_case_multi('HELLO. HOW ARE you.') == 'Hello. How are you.'
hidden_tests: assert sentence_case_multi('FIRST. SECOND. THIRD.') == 'First. Second. Third.'
assert sentence_case_multi('a. b. c.') == 'A. B. C.'
assert sentence_case_multi('ALL CAPS. still caps.') == 'All caps. Still caps.'
assert sentence_case_multi('no periods at all here') == 'No periods at all here'
assert sentence_case_multi('MIXED case. Another ONE.') == 'Mixed case. Another one.'
assert sentence_case_multi('   . text after dot') == '   . Text after dot'
assert sentence_case_multi('one. TWO. three. FOUR.') == 'One. Two. Three. Four.'
assert sentence_case_multi('. leading dot') == '. Leading dot'
assert sentence_case_multi('what. now. THIS.') == 'What. Now. This.'
assert sentence_case_multi('A. B. C. D.') == 'A. B. C. D.'
assert sentence_case_multi('test. TEST. Test.') == 'Test. Test. Test.'

family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: Split text on newline characters. For each non-empty line, lowercase it and then uppercase its first alphabetic character (a line with no letters stays fully lowered). Lines that are completely empty are left as empty strings. Rejoin all lines with newline characters.

family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: Apply sentence casing to s (lowercase the whole string, then uppercase its first alphabetic character). Then split the result on single spaces and, for any word that matches (ignoring case) one of the given acronym strings, replace it with that acronym's exact given form; other words keep their sentence-cased form. Rejoin the words with single spaces.
visible_tests: assert sentence_case_preserve_acronyms('the nasa mission launched', ['NASA']) == 'The NASA mission launched'
assert sentence_case_preserve_acronyms('visit the usa today', ['USA']) == 'Visit the USA today'
hidden_tests: assert sentence_case_preserve_acronyms('the fbi and cia work together', ['FBI', 'CIA']) == 'The FBI and CIA work together'
assert sentence_case_preserve_acronyms('no acronyms here at all', ['XYZ']) == 'No acronyms here at all'
assert sentence_case_preserve_acronyms('ALREADY CAPS nasa TEXT', ['NASA']) == 'Already caps NASA text'
assert sentence_case_preserve_acronyms('the abc and def and ghi', ['ABC', 'DEF', 'GHI']) == 'The ABC and DEF and GHI'
assert sentence_case_preserve_acronyms('edge case with usa usa usa', ['USA']) == 'Edge case with USA USA USA'
assert sentence_case_preserve_acronyms('MIXED case nasa mission', ['NASA']) == 'Mixed case NASA mission'
assert sentence_case_preserve_acronyms('nothing matches here', []) == 'Nothing matches here'
assert sentence_case_preserve_acronyms('first word nasa', ['NASA']) == 'First word NASA'
assert sentence_case_preserve_acronyms('the un and who reported', ['UN', 'WHO']) == 'The UN and WHO reported'
assert sentence_case_preserve_acronyms('repeated fbi fbi fbi', ['FBI']) == 'Repeated FBI FBI FBI'
assert sentence_case_preserve_acronyms('case insensitive NaSa test', ['NASA']) == 'Case insensitive NASA test'
assert sentence_case_preserve_acronyms('multi acronym cia fbi usa test', ['CIA', 'FBI', 'USA']) == 'Multi acronym CIA FBI USA test'
assert sentence_case_preserve_acronyms('no match nasax here', ['NASA']) == 'No match nasax here'

family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: Replace every character in the given filename that is not a letter, digit, hyphen, underscore, or period with an underscore, leaving allowed characters untouched.

family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: First replace every space character in the filename with an underscore, then remove any remaining character that is not a letter, digit, underscore, period, or hyphen (do not replace them, just drop them).

family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: Lowercase the filename and replace every space with a hyphen, then remove any character that is not a lowercase letter, digit, hyphen, or period.

family: simple text formatting (padding, wrapping, title-casing, abbreviations, slugs)
spec: If the filename's total length is already at most max_len, return it unchanged. Otherwise, if the filename contains a period, split it into a base name and extension at the last period, shorten the base name so that the base plus the (dot-included) extension fits exactly within max_len characters, and return that combination; if the extension alone is longer than max_len, just cut the whole original filename to max_len characters. If there is no period at all, simply cut the filename to the first max_len characters.
